text: A warning whose only working containment is that people stop reading at it, written by an office that knows exactly this.

text: A record that can be neither deleted nor redacted, so the procedure protecting everyone from it is a politely worded request.

text: The perimeter is a national law and a waste-disposal cover story, and the standing order for anything inside it is to fire.

title: setting-b

text: Damnation with an entry standard: those judged insufficiently wicked are turned away and left half-alive at the gate until the end of days, so failure has no floor.

text: A tithe paid in skilled people rather than coin, so the annual return from each nation is a list of names and the shortfall is a man who did not arrive.

text: Holy super-soldiers rented to the highest bidder because the war needs the money, so sanctity has a rate card and the poorest sector fights without it.

text: The dead claimed by neither side when they fall near something holy, obeying orders nobody living can hear, so the safest ground is the one that manufactures them.

text: Hell as a functioning polity with a committee, a majority vote and constant turnover, so the defenders survive on the enemy's gridlock and know exactly how long that lasts.

text: One exemption code that covers worlds too holy to tax and worlds that no longer exist, so the system cannot tell a shrine from a grave and stopped needing to.

text: A world lost not to the enemy but in the records, alive, unaddressed, still filing returns nobody receives, and the correct way to find it is to file something.

text: A unit destroyed and raised again under the same number with its honours inherited, so the institution is immortal because its members are interchangeable, and they find this consoling.

text: A harvest on a hundred-year rotation with quotas, receipts and inspections, feeding a corpse so that ships can find their way home, and nobody's atrocity.

text: A soldier as the temporary container for two glands that carry someone else's lineage, so the medic on the field is recovering assets and the dying man agrees.

text: A sentence reserved for those who retain hope of redemption: the mind removed, the head filled with hymns, and the kindness real, doctrinally motivated, and the last step before the trigger.

text: A ship still executing an order cut a thousand years ago by an office that no longer exists, not lost or haunted but compliant, and someone will have to receive its report.

text: A reformer who is right, holds absolute authority, and cannot act because the false account is now structural and the true one is heresy.

text: Writing continued after the pencil stopped marking, because the record was the obligation and legibility never was.

text: An archive sealed with one person inside for the duration, and the duration is set by what is happening above, which nobody will measure again.

text: A stranger who selects you at an empty counter, and the selection turns out to be a property of you rather than of him.

text: A town where the arrangement is known to everyone old enough, maintained by not being discussed, and it works.

text: An heirloom that cannot be disposed of because every method returns it, and the returning is unremarkable to those who have tried.

text: Crossing a stretch of frozen water because it is the way home, and being met there by everyone who crossed before.
